findings.title: Prior HIGH finding (guest-writable channel directory permitting a symlink swap the host would dereference) is closed and independently reproven with a broader attack surface
findings.evidence: Live sandboxed-guest PoC (/tmp/factory-platform-evidence/w01-revalidation2/logs/live-guest-attack-poc.log) against the exact shipped runnerChannelMount()/args() flags: unlink, rename, symlink-swap, regular-file-create, directory-create, and (new vs. both the prior validator's PoC and the worker's own test) hardlink and fchmod all return EROFS, while the read-write FIFO open succeeds and the host-side entry's inode is unchanged after the attack. Code reading confirms the identity check (O_NOFOLLOW + fstat + recorded dev/ino match, facts stored outside the mounted directory) is applied through one shared private method used identically on initial launch and on every attach/recovery, closing the 'unconditionally reachable via recovery' concern the prior validator raised.

findings.title: The design addendum and G17's gate evidence overstate the typed-error guarantee; a symlink or directory substituted for a channel entry is refused by a raw OS error, not by RunnerError('channel_untrusted', ...)
findings.location: packages/@ezcorp/extension-runner/src/podman.ts:184-199 (openChannelEntry); tasks/factory/w01-GATES.md G17 evidence ('refusing anything else with a typed channel_untrusted error'); /tmp/factory-platform-evidence/w01/DESIGN-guest-lifetime.md addendum ('Anything else is refused with a typed channel_untrusted error')
findings.description: open(path, flags | O_NOFOLLOW) throws a raw Node fs error (ELOOP for a symlink, EISDIR for a directory) before the function's own fstat/identity check ever executes; only a type-mismatch that survives open() -- a regular file swapped in for the FIFO -- reaches the isFIFO()/dev/ino comparison and gets the typed RunnerError. Reproduced directly against the shipped private method in /tmp/factory-platform-evidence/w01-revalidation2/logs/host-identity-poc.log: symlink -> 'ELOOP: too many symbolic links encountered' (not channel_untrusted); directory -> 'EISDIR' (not channel_untrusted); regular file -> RunnerError('channel_untrusted', 'Runner control channel entry is not the FIFO the runner created') as claimed. This is not a security bypass -- every attack vector is still refused unconditionally, confirmed live in finding 1 -- and no caller in the codebase pattern-matches on the 'channel_untrusted' code (grep found only the four throw sites), so nothing downstream currently depends on the distinction. The worker's own channel-identity.test.ts quietly reflects this: its symlink case asserts only `.rejects.toThrow()` with no message check, while every other case in that file asserts the specific message text. Remediation: wrap the open() call in openChannelEntry() in a try/catch and rethrow any failure as RunnerError('channel_untrusted', ...), which would make the claim in the design addendum and G17 literally true, or correct the addendum/gate prose to state precisely which failure mode applies to which substitution.

findings.title: The identity check's collision resistance depends on the filesystem not reusing a freed inode number; this only matters if the (independently proven robust) primary read-only-mount barrier were ever defeated by some other means
findings.description: Attempting to construct a 'FIFO recreated with a genuinely different real inode' test case (as opposed to the worker's own test, which correctly edits the recorded facts file directly rather than relying on recreation) found that unlink+mkfifo at the same path immediately reused the exact same kernel inode number on this host's filesystem, both times tried (/tmp/factory-platform-evidence/w01-revalidation2/logs/host-identity-poc.log, case 'recreated-fifo-real-different-inode-refused'). This is a filesystem behavior observation, not a reachable exploit: production's read-only bind mount and 0o755 directory (proven live in finding 1, including against hardlink and directory-create attempts my own broader PoC added) already prevent the guest from ever unlinking or recreating a channel entry in the first place, so this only becomes relevant if that primary barrier is bypassed by an unrelated defect. Noting it as a documentation point for the design record: the device+inode identity check is a second, independent, but not on-its-own collision-proof layer; recording it as defense-in-depth rather than a self-sufficient control would be more precise. No action required to accept this delta.
